  WHY: Two reviewers said this was already resolved, but two reviewers still report stale introductory wording that can mislead readers about the current limits.

  flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_1-fast]

  WHY: The comment is documentation-only, but a drifting reference can send maintainers to the wrong place when they revisit the timeout sizing rationale.
- scripts/review_conflict_resolve.sh:390-420 | severity=low | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_1-fast]
  PROBLEM: The header comment still describes a single prelude template and fail-open path, but `_build_retry_prompt` now selects among validation, timeout, and exec_error paths.
  WHY: The comment is stale and can mislead maintainers debugging why a particular prelude path was rendered or skipped.
- scripts/review_conflict_resolve.sh:472-485 | severity=low | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_1-fast]
  PROBLEM: The placeholder-derivation logic can leave new template variables unsubstituted if they do not match the current regex/key assumptions.
  WHY: If a future template introduces an unrecognized placeholder, codex receives the literal `{{...}}` text and may follow the wrong instructions.
- scripts/review_conflict_resolve.sh:597-600 | severity=low | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_1-fast]
  PROBLEM: The comment describing `_prev_attempt_failure_kind` does not accurately reflect that exit 137 is only classified as timeout when elapsed time meets the budget and that exec_error falls back to a verbatim prompt.
  WHY: The comment can mislead readers tracing why a 137 exit routes to the exec_error path.
- scripts/review_conflict_resolve.sh:806-811 | severity=low | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_6-plus]
  PROBLEM: The elapsed-time check uses whole-second `date +%s` arithmetic, so a genuine timeout near the budget boundary can be misclassified as exec_error.
  WHY: This can send the next retry down the wrong prelude path even though the attempt was actually killed for timing out.
- tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py:6785-6824 | severity=low | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_1-fast]
  PROBLEM: The test’s `close_re` slicing assumes the first standalone `)` closes the array, which can select the wrong body if an earlier line matches that pattern.
  WHY: A refactor could invalidate the allowlist assertion without the test catching it, leaving the timeout-prelude staging contract unverified.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
